name: Zircon

matrix.title: Pupin (1980) typology grid
matrix.subtitle: Columns: I.A, the pyramid index, which reflects melt Al/(Na+K). Rows: I.T, the prism index, which Pupin read as a crystallization temperature.
matrix.note: The layout follows Pupin (1980, Fig. 1) as reproduced by Osorio-Granada et al. (2017) and Daneshvar et al. (2018). The temperature scale is Pupin's ±50 °C estimate. Mixed steps are spaced evenly as 1/6–5/6 of the prism perimeter or pyramid area. Pupin's ratios are visual, so this spacing is a modelling choice and not part of the original definition. Prismatic types are drawn at 2.5:1 and the {301} types at 3.6:1.

about:
Pupin (1980) sorted accessory zircon from granitoids into 64 cells (S1–S25, L, G, P, Q, R, J, AB and the single-letter types) using two indices.

  • I.A (columns) records the relative development of the pyramids {211} and {101}, plus the steep {301}. Pupin read it as an index of the melt's Al/(Na+K) balance.
  • I.T (rows) records the prisms, from none, to {110} only, to {100} only. Pupin read it as a crystallization temperature from about 550 to 900 °C.

The mean point (Ā, T̄) and the typological evolution trend of a zircon population fall in fields for crustal, hybrid and mantle-derived granites.

Every crystal in the matrix uses the real zircon cell (c/a = 0.905), so all interfacial angles are genuine zircon angles. Only the central distances of the five forms change from cell to cell. The temperature reading of I.T is contested. Benisek & Finger (1993) showed that trace-element uptake on {110} also controls prism development, so use the T axis as Pupin's calibration, not as a thermometer.

habits.name: Crustal (aluminous) granites
habits.text: Low I.A, about 150–350, and I.T about 300–450. S1–S7, L and Q types dominate: {211}-rich pyramids on {110}-rich prisms. This covers aluminous leucogranites and (sub)autochthonous and intrusive aluminous monzogranites and granodiorites.

habits.name: Hybrid (crust + mantle) granites
habits.text: Calc-alkaline and high-K calc-alkaline granodiorites and monzonites at I.A about 400–550, spanning about 650–850 °C. Subalkaline granites at I.A about 550–650, up to about 870 °C.

habits.name: Mantle-derived granites
habits.text: High I.A: {101}-dominated pyramids, the P, J and D types. Alkaline granites at I.A about 650–720 over about 550–890 °C. Tholeiitic granites at I.A about 700 and about 900 °C.

habits.name: Special markers
habits.text: Charnockites (Ch) plot at about 850–875 °C and I.A about 300–450. The muscovite-granite limit (Mu) lies near I.T 450, about 725 °C. Field positions are read from redrawn figures and are good to about ±50 index units.

references.citation: Pupin, J.P. (1980). Zircon and granite petrology. Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology 73, 207–220.
references.note: The typology reproduced in this matrix, with the I.A/I.T indices, 64 subtypes and petrogenetic fields.

references.citation: Pupin, J.P., Turco, G. (1972). Une typologie originale du zircon accessoire. Bulletin de la Société française de Minéralogie et de Cristallographie 95, 348–359.
references.note: The original (French) version of the typology chart.

references.citation: Pupin, J.P., Bonin, B., Tessier, M., Turco, G. (1978). Rôle de l'eau sur les caractères morphologiques et la cristallisation du zircon dans les granitoïdes. Bulletin de la Société Géologique de France S7-XX(5), 721–725.
references.note: Melt water content as an additional control on zircon habit.

references.citation: Pupin, J.P., Turco, G. (1976). Occurrence of peculiar tabular zircon crystals. Mineralogical Magazine 40, 790–792.
references.note: Rare {001}-bearing tabular habit, which lies outside the 64-cell grid.

references.citation: Vavra, G. (1990). On the kinematics of zircon growth and its petrogenetic significance: a cathodoluminescence study. Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology 106, 90–99.
references.note: Growth-sector kinematics from CL. Habit changes during growth and is not a single equilibrium state.

references.citation: Vavra, G. (1993). A guide to quantitative morphology of accessory zircon. Chemical Geology 110, 15–28.
references.note: Quantitative morphology from relative face growth rates, the closest published analogue to the central-distance approach used here.

references.citation: Vavra, G. (1994). Systematics of internal zircon morphology in major Variscan granitoid types. Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology 117, 331–344.
Benisek, A., Finger, F. (1993). Factors controlling the development of prism faces in granite zircons: a microprobe study. Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology 114, 441–451.
references.note: The main critique of the I.T thermometer: trace elements (U, Th, Y) taken up on prism faces affect {100}/{110} development.

references.citation: Belousova, E.A., Griffin, W.L., O'Reilly, S.Y. (2006). Zircon crystal morphology, trace element signatures and Hf isotope composition as a tool for petrogenetic modelling: examples from Eastern Australian granitoids. Journal of Petrology 47, 329–353.
references.note: Pupin-type morphology combined with trace elements and Hf isotopes.

references.citation: Vavra, G., Schmid, R., Gebauer, D. (1999). Internal morphology, habit and U-Th-Pb microanalysis of amphibolite-to-granulite facies zircons: geochronology of the Ivrea Zone. Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology 134, 380–404.
references.note: Metamorphic zircon habits (equant, multifaceted) that fall outside the igneous typology.

references.citation: Corfu, F., Hanchar, J.M., Hoskin, P.W.O., Kinny, P. (2003). Atlas of zircon textures. Reviews in Mineralogy and Geochemistry 53, 469–500.
references.note: The standard imaging reference for zircon habit and internal textures.

references.citation: Watson, E.B., Harrison, T.M. (1983). Zircon saturation revisited: temperature and composition effects in a variety of crustal magma types. Earth and Planetary Science Letters 64, 295–304.
references.note: The independent zircon-saturation temperature, often compared with Pupin's I.T.

references.citation: Hourigan, J.K., Reiners, P.W., Brandon, M.T. (2005). U-Th zonation-dependent alpha-ejection in (U-Th)/He chronometry. Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta 69, 3349–3365.
references.note: F<sub>T</sub> corrections for tetragonal prisms with pyramidal terminations, the geometry modelled here.

references.citation: Zeigler, S.D., Baker, M., Metcalf, J.R., Flowers, R.M. (2024). The Geometric Correction Method for zircon (U–Th)/He chronology. Geochronology 6, 199–226.
references.note: Compares 2D measurements with 3D nano-CT on 223 zircons. 2D geometry overestimates volume and F<sub>T</sub>.

references.citation: Osorio-Granada, E., Restrepo-Moreno, S.A., Muñoz-Valencia, J.A., Trejos-Tamayo, R.A., Pardo-Trujillo, A., Barbosa-Espitia, A.A. (2017). Detrital zircon typology and U/Pb geochronology for the Miocene Ladrilleros-Juanchaco sedimentary sequence, Equatorial Pacific (Colombia). Geologica Acta 15(3), 201–215.
references.note: Fig. 4 is an English-labelled reproduction of Pupin's chart, used here for the grid layout.

references.citation: Daneshvar, N., Maanijou, M., Azizi, H., Asahara, Y. (2018). Study of the zircon morphology and internal structures as a tool for constraining magma source: example from granitoid bodies in the northern Sanandaj Sirjan zone (SW Saqqez). Geopersia 8(2), 245–259.
references.note: Figs. 5–6 reproduce the original French chart and the petrogenetic fields, used here for the grid layout.

references.citation: Robinson, K., Gibbs, G.V., Ribbe, P.H. (1971). The structure of zircon: a comparison with garnet. American Mineralogist 56, 782–790.
references.note: The source of the zircon cell used here (a = 6.607, c = 5.982 Å).

cells.label: B
cells.title: B: I.A 100, I.T 100
cells.description: I.A = 100: {211} only. I.T = 100: no prism (~550 °C after Pupin 1980).

cells.label: A
cells.title: A: I.A 700, I.T 100
cells.description: I.A = 700: {101} only. I.T = 100: no prism (~550 °C after Pupin 1980).

cells.label: C
cells.title: C: I.A 800, I.T 100
cells.description: I.A = 800: {301}. I.T = 100: no prism (~550 °C after Pupin 1980).

cells.label: G1
cells.title: G1: I.A 700, I.T 200
cells.description: I.A = 700: {101} only. I.T = 200: {110} only (~600 °C after Pupin 1980). G2 and G3 (small, near-equant variants in the same cell) are not modelled.
